references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Where a Secondary dwelling is proposed on a lot containing an existing Dwelling house, the development is considered to be a Material Change of Use because it increases the intensity and scale of the use of the premises. A Dwelling house (which can include a Secondary dwelling) is generally accepted development subject to requirements in Residential zones. The level of assessment for each zone is in Part 5 of CairnsPlan 2016.
references.interpretation: Adding a secondary dwelling to a lot with a house is a material change of use; whether it needs a development application depends on the zone's table of assessment (not encoded). Captured on 2026-10-09 from an automated summary of the published document; the exact wording was not available. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Secondary dwelling size limits under CairnsPlan 2016: Rural zone, 250 m2 on lots over 10 ha or 70 m2 on lots under 10 ha. Low density residential, Low-medium density residential, Medium density residential, Rural residential and Tourist accommodation zones (excluding Tourist accommodation precinct 1, islands): 70 m2. All other zones on lots over 450 m2: 70 m2.
references.interpretation: Floor area limits by zone and lot size. No limit is stated for other zones on lots of 450 m2 or less, or for rural lots of exactly 10 ha. Captured on 2026-10-09 from an automated summary of the published document; the exact wording was not available. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Parking: a Dual occupancy needs 4 spaces in total; a Secondary dwelling (with its Dwelling house) needs 3. A Dual occupancy's dwellings can be leased and serviced separately and get separate addresses, letterboxes and bins; a Secondary dwelling shares these with the main dwelling.
references.interpretation: Three car parking spaces in total for a house with a secondary dwelling. references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Reconfiguring a lot includes creating lots by subdividing another lot. Reconfiguring a lot that is code or impact assessable under Part 5 of CairnsPlan 2016 requires an application for a development permit. Approvals may be conditioned (access, building envelopes, geotechnical matters, service connections, infrastructure works, staging, further studies). Application fees are in council's Fees and Charges Schedule, and infrastructure charges apply to reconfiguring a lot.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Dwelling houses are generally accepted development subject to the zone and Hillslopes overlay requirements; a proposal that does not meet them needs a development application. Development does not occur on land with a gradient in excess of 1 in 6 (16.6%). Excavation and filling no more than 50 m3; batters and retaining walls no higher than 1.8 m each; earthworks at least 2 m from boundaries. Possible conditions include geotechnical certification.
references.interpretation: Steep sites in the Hillslopes overlay have strict limits; failing them needs a development application. The overlay itself comes from council's mapping (not looked up). references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] From 26 September 2022 (Planning (Secondary Dwellings) Amendment Regulation 2022): 'household' means 1 or more individuals who live together in a dwelling; 'secondary dwelling' means a dwelling on a lot that is used in conjunction with, but subordinate to, another dwelling. The definitions no longer require a secondary dwelling to be occupied by members of the same household as the main dwelling.
references.interpretation: A secondary dwelling can be occupied by anyone, including renters unrelated to the main household. rule_sets.title: Cairns: secondary dwellings
rule_sets.description: Secondary dwellings (granny flats) in the Cairns Regional Council area, from council's CairnsPlan 2016 fact sheet and the Planning Regulation 2017.
limitations: Built from Cairns Regional Council fact sheets last updated in October 2021, not from the full text of CairnsPlan 2016, which has been amended since.
Does not check the zone's table of assessment (CairnsPlan 2016 Part 5), overlays other than steep land, or the dwelling house code (setbacks, height, site cover).
Does not cover Tourist accommodation zone precinct 1 (islands), which the fact sheet excludes from the 70 m2 limit.
The council area and zone come from your answers. We do not look them up.
Not legal advice. Confirm with Cairns Regional Council or a town planner before you rely on it.

rules.title: Adding a secondary dwelling to a lot with a house
rules.notes: Capped at likely: the fact sheet is guidance and the zone's level of assessment is not encoded.

outcomes.title: This is a material change of use, so a development application may be needed
outcomes.detail: Cairns Regional Council's fact sheet says a secondary dwelling on a lot that already has a house is a material change of use. Whether that needs a development application depends on the zone's table of assessment in Part 5 of CairnsPlan 2016, which we have not checked. Ask council or a town planner to confirm.

approval.pathway: Level of assessment set by the zone (CairnsPlan 2016 Part 5)

payload.task: Ask Cairns Regional Council whether the secondary dwelling needs a development application

outcomes.title: Building the secondary dwelling with a new house
outcomes.detail: A dwelling house can include a secondary dwelling. Council's fact sheet says a dwelling house is generally accepted development subject to requirements in residential zones; if the design doesn't meet those requirements, an application is needed.

rules.title: Building approval for a secondary dwelling

outcomes.title: Building approval is needed for the building work
outcomes.detail: Council's fact sheet says you need a building works approval for any building works, as well as any planning approval. A building certifier assesses and issues it.

evidence.title: Building plans for the secondary dwelling

payload.task: Engage a building certifier for the building approval

rules.title: Secondary dwelling size
rules.notes: MATCH means within a limit the fact sheet states. NO_MATCH covers both 'over the limit' and 'no limit stated' (other zones on lots of 450 m2 or less, rural lots of exactly 10 ha).

outcomes.title: Within the size council's fact sheet gives for a secondary dwelling
outcomes.detail: The fact sheet limits a secondary dwelling to 70 m2 in most zones, or 250 m2 on rural lots over 10 ha. Check how council measures floor area before you rely on this.

outcomes.title: Larger than council's fact sheet allows, or no limit is stated for this zone and lot size
outcomes.detail: A second home that is too big to be a secondary dwelling may be treated differently, for example as a dual occupancy, which has its own rules (council's fact sheet gives minimum lot sizes of 600 m2 or 800 m2). Talk to council or a town planner.

payload.task: Check the secondary dwelling's size with council or a town planner

rules.title: Car parking for a secondary dwelling

outcomes.title: Show three car parks on your site plan
outcomes.detail: Council's fact sheet says a house with a secondary dwelling needs 3 car parking spaces in total (a dual occupancy needs 4).

evidence.title: Site plan showing three car parking spaces
evidence.detail: Show where each car parks, including the spaces for the main house.

rules.title: Who can live in a secondary dwelling
rules.notes: Council's 2021 fact sheet still describes the same-household rule that the state removed in 2022.

outcomes.title: A secondary dwelling can be rented to anyone
outcomes.detail: Since 26 September 2022 the Planning Regulation 2017 no longer requires a secondary dwelling to be lived in by the same household as the main house. Council's 2021 fact sheet still describes the older rule. Approvals with occupancy conditions may need a change application, and the change doesn't remove the need for any approval.

rule_sets.title: Cairns: subdivision (reconfiguring a lot)
rule_sets.description: Subdividing land in the Cairns Regional Council area, from council's CairnsPlan 2016 reconfiguring a lot fact sheet.
limitations: Built from Cairns Regional Council's reconfiguring a lot fact sheet (last updated October 2021), not from the full text of CairnsPlan 2016, which has been amended since.
Minimum lot sizes are only known for the Low density and Low-medium density residential zones. Part 9 of CairnsPlan 2016 has the rest.
Does not check state referrals, access, services, overlays or the survey plan process.
The council area and zone come from your answers. We do not look them up.
Not legal advice. Confirm with Cairns Regional Council or a town planner before you rely on it.

rules.title: Development permit for subdividing
rules.notes: Capped at likely: the level of assessment (Part 5) is not encoded.

outcomes.title: A development permit for reconfiguring a lot is likely to be needed
outcomes.detail: Council's fact sheet says subdividing is reconfiguring a lot, and that it needs a development permit application where Part 5 of CairnsPlan 2016 makes it code or impact assessable. We have not checked Part 5 for your zone, so confirm the level of assessment with council.

approval.pathway: Development permit (code or impact assessment under CairnsPlan 2016 Part 5)

evidence.title: Proposal plan showing the new lots, their areas and frontages

payload.task: Confirm the level of assessment for the subdivision with Cairns Regional Council

rules.title: Minimum lot size
rules.notes: MATCH means every new lot meets the minimum the fact sheet states. NO_MATCH covers 'below it' and 'no minimum stated for this zone'. Small lot provisions (350 m2) are not encoded.

outcomes.title: The proposed lots meet the minimum size in council's fact sheet
outcomes.detail: Low density residential: 600 m2 and 15 m wide. Low-medium density residential: 450 m2. The other requirements in Part 9 of CairnsPlan 2016 still apply.

outcomes.title: Below the minimum lot size in council's fact sheet, or no minimum is stated for this zone
outcomes.detail: In the Low-medium density residential zone, lots down to 350 m2 may be possible where the small lot provisions are met. Part 9 of CairnsPlan 2016 has the minimum for every zone.

payload.task: Check the proposed lot sizes against Part 9 of CairnsPlan 2016

outcomes.title: Application fees and infrastructure charges apply
outcomes.detail: Council's fact sheet says infrastructure charges apply to reconfiguring a lot, on top of the application fee in council's fees and charges schedule. We don't calculate either.

payload.task: Ask Cairns Regional Council for the application fee and an infrastructure charges estimate

rule_sets.title: Cairns: steep land (Hillslopes overlay)
rule_sets.description: Houses, extensions and secondary dwellings on steep land in the Cairns Regional Council area.
limitations: We only know about steep land if you tell us. Council's overlay mapping decides whether the Hillslopes overlay applies.
Built from council's Hillslopes overlay fact sheet for dwelling houses (last updated October 2021).

rules.title: Steep land and the Hillslopes overlay
rules.notes: Only fires when the customer ticks steep slope. An empty answer stays unknown on purpose: we never assume a site is flat.

outcomes.title: Steep land: the Hillslopes overlay may apply
outcomes.detail: Council's fact sheet for dwelling houses in the Hillslopes overlay says development does not occur on land steeper than 1 in 6 (16.6%), and limits earthworks (no more than 50 m3 of cut or fill, batters and retaining walls no higher than 1.8 m). Work that doesn't meet these needs a development application. Check council's overlay mapping for your site.

approval.pathway: Development application if the Hillslopes overlay requirements are not met

payload.task: Check council's Hillslopes overlay mapping for the site
